newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady with some active short-end buying by traders squaring off their positions, dealers said on Monday.
"The market saw some active short-end buying this afternoon just to square off their books," a local dealer said.
He added some traders are also looking towards to tonight's release of the U.S. consumer credit data for August.
"But I don't think these figures will have a great impact on the market," he said.
The U.S. average consumer credit figure was forecast at US$7.3 billion compared to the previous $7.7 billion.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday and Tuesday/Wednesday remained steady at a common 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent.
Week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/4 5-1/8 percent from Friday's 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent, three-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months and five-months rose 1/16 percentage point to a common 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent.
Twelve-months rose 2/16 percentage point to 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent from Friday's 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
